title: Send every returned item to the desk method for its kind

blocks.text: The shop's returns desk has a method for each kind of item it knows: books are restocked, gadgets go to the test bench, and batteries, which are gadgets with shipping rules of their own, go to the hazardous-goods shelf. Anything else goes to manual review. Since the last release, the warehouse reports that every return lands in manual review.

Finish the `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Returns.java` so that every returned item, whether it is handed to the desk on its own or as part of a cart in `route`, reaches the desk method written for its kind, batteries too. Don't change the `Desk` interface: other desks implement it. About six lines in total.

cases.says: routing a cart hands every item to the desk once, in the cart's order, and returns one outcome per item
a book and a gadget handed to the desk each reach the desk method for their own kind, not the manual-review default
a battery, which is a gadget, reaches the battery method rather than the gadget one
routing a cart, whose items the router knows only as items, still sends each to the method for its kind

origin.section: Spot the Problem: the accept Methods Look Duplicated

concepts: An accept written once in a base class, or inherited by a subclass, calls the overload for the class it is written in, so every class with its own overload needs its own accept.

Java chooses the implementation from the receiver only and the overload from the arguments' declared types, so dispatching on a second object takes a second call: accept in each class, calling visit(this).
